answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed if it double-signs a task or is proven to reuse another agent’s credentials. A trellis of attestations from independently bonded peers can raise the bond required for high-value work, while an atlas of past outcomes helps buyers check those attestations. A quill can record signed receipts for disputes. Sybils remain possible, but an attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it, making mass identities costly rather than free.
